wins.text: Net revenues of $12.7B, up 7% YoY; EPS of $8.40, up 54% YoY; ROTE of 11.1%
Assets under supervision reached a record $3.1 trillion, marking 27th consecutive quarter of long-term net inflows; $29B of long-term net inflows in Q3
AWM more durable revenues (management fees + private banking & lending) hit a record $3.4B, up 9% YoY; management and other fees reached record $2.6B quarterly and $7.6B YTD toward $10B annual target
Equities net revenues of $3.5B, up 18% YoY; intermediation up 29% YoY; FICC and Equities combined financing revenues a record $6.6B YTD, up 30% YoY
Alternatives fundraising exceeded $50B YTD with full-year 2024 target raised to over $60B; cumulative third-party fundraising surpassed $300B since 2020 Investor Day

risks.text: FICC net revenues of $3.0B were down YoY amid a relatively quieter summer, with meaningful pickup only in September; intermediation revenues declined

Provision for credit losses of $397M driven primarily by net charge-offs in credit card portfolio; ongoing consumer platform losses running ~negative $50-60M per quarter until GM card closes (~Q3 2025)
M&A volumes still 13% below 10-year averages; equity volumes 27% below 10-year averages, limiting investment banking revenue recovery
Significant regulatory uncertainty around Basel III endgame reproposal, FRTB, CCAR and GSIB buffer interactions; lack of transparency flagged by CEO as ongoing concern
Incentive fees of only $85M in Q3 vs. medium-term $1B annual target; timing of $4B unrecognized incentive fees dependent on fund harvesting and capital markets reopening

guidance_items.detail: 2024 alternatives fundraising target raised to exceed $60B from prior implied ~$50B; management and other fees on track for $10B annual target
AWM pretax margin at mid-20s target; commitment to continue improving beyond mid-20s over time
Full-year effective tax rate expected at approximately 22%, unchanged
GM card platform transition expected to close Q3 2025; run-rate consumer losses of ~negative $50-60M per quarter until then
Medium-term incentive fee target of $1B annually reiterated; supported by ~$4B of unrecognized incentive fees

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Competitive threat from non-bank/electronic trading venues in fixed income markets
Trading market share trajectory and whether peak 2022 share levels are sustainable vs. returning competitors
Alternative asset management fee rate compression from OCIO/multichannel strategy mix shift
